def _mint_hmac_secret(
    channel: NotificationChannel, secret_store: SecretStore, *, previous_ref: str | None = None
) -> str:
    """Generate a fresh HMAC signing key and store it — rotating in place when
    ``previous_ref`` names an existing ref (the old value there is replaced,
    then explicitly purged), the same tri-state rotation contract every other
    webhook secret on this table uses via `apply_secret_webhook`.
    """
    hmac_secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    channel.hmac_secret_ref, cleared = notification_service.apply_secret_webhook(
        hmac_secret,
        previous_ref,
        ref_prefix="channel-hmac",
        config_id=channel.id,
        secret_store=secret_store,
    )
    if cleared:
        secret_store.delete(cleared)
    return hmac_secret

def _mint_channel_secret(
    channel: NotificationChannel,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
    *,
    value: str,
    ref_attr: str,
    ref_prefix: str,
) -> str:
    """Store ``value`` at whichever ref column ``ref_attr`` names — rotating in
    place when the channel already has a ref there (the old value is
    replaced, then explicitly purged), the tri-state rotation contract every
    secret-bearing channel field shares via `apply_secret_webhook`. Shared by
    every channel secret (HMAC key, auth-header value) so a bug in the
    rotate-and-purge sequence is fixed once, not once per field.
    """
    new_ref, cleared = notification_service.apply_secret_webhook(
        value,
        getattr(channel, ref_attr),
        ref_prefix=ref_prefix,
        config_id=channel.id,
        secret_store=secret_store,
    )
    setattr(channel, ref_attr, new_ref)
    if cleared:
        secret_store.delete(cleared)
    return value


def _mint_hmac_secret(channel: NotificationChannel, secret_store: SecretStore) -> str:
    """Generate a fresh HMAC signing key and store it."""
    return _mint_channel_secret(
        channel,
        secret_store,
        value=secrets.token_urlsafe(32),
        ref_attr="hmac_secret_ref",
        ref_prefix="channel-hmac",
    )

99	_MISSING = object()
100	_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{\{\s*([\w.]+)\s*\}\}")

103	def _resolve_path(payload: dict[str, Any], path: str) -> Any:
104	    """Resolve a dot-path (list indices are numeric segments) against the
105	    already-redacted generic payload — a pure key/index lookup, nothing else,
106	    so a path can only ever reach a field the payload already exposes.
107	    """
108	    current: Any = payload
109	    for segment in path.split("."):
110	        if isinstance(current, dict):
111	            if segment not in current:
112	                return _MISSING
113	            current = current[segment]
114	        elif isinstance(current, list):
115	            if not segment.isdigit() or not (0 <= int(segment) < len(current)):
116	                return _MISSING
117	            current = current[int(segment)]
118	        else:
119	            return _MISSING
120	    return current

123	def _render_template_value(node: Any, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
124	    if isinstance(node, str):
125	        stripped = node.strip()
126	        exact = _PLACEHOLDER.fullmatch(stripped)
127	        if exact:
128	            # The whole string IS one placeholder — substitute the raw
129	            # resolved value (preserving its type: a number/bool/object/None,
130	            # not a stringified copy), so a template can produce e.g. a JSON
131	            # number or nested object field, not just text.
132	            resolved = _resolve_path(payload, exact.group(1))
133	            return None if resolved is _MISSING else resolved
134	
135	        def _interpolate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
136	            resolved = _resolve_path(payload, match.group(1))
137	            return "" if resolved is _MISSING else str(resolved)
138	
139	        return _PLACEHOLDER.sub(_interpolate, node)
140	    if isinstance(node, dict):
141	        return {key: _render_template_value(value, payload) for key, value in node.items()}
142	    if isinstance(node, list):
143	        return [_render_template_value(item, payload) for item in node]
144	    return node  # int/float/bool/None literals pass through unchanged

148	    """Render a channel's custom payload template (#1663) against the already-
149	    redacted generic-webhook payload. A placeholder (``{{field.path}}``)
150	    resolves by KEY LOOKUP ONLY — there is no expression language, no code
151	    execution — so a template can rename/reshape/select the fields
152	    ``render_webhook_payload`` already exposes, and never reach anything it
153	    doesn't (the #1118/#1401 "no new exfiltration primitive" class). An
154	    unresolvable path degrades to ``null``/empty-string rather than raising —
155	    a template referencing a field this particular run doesn't have (e.g. no
156	    incidents) must not break delivery.
157	    """
158	    return {key: _render_template_value(value, payload) for key, value in template.items()}

168	    `publish_poll_staleness` (workspace-wide signals) are therefore honest

170	    a channel type with no workspace concept could ever carry them.
171	    """

class ChannelRead(ApiModel):
    """A channel's shape as any authenticated caller may see it. The Teams/Slack
    webhook and the generic webhook's HMAC signing key are credentials and
    never returned, only whether one is set — `webhook_url` is the exception:
    for a generic webhook it is the destination, not the credential (the HMAC
    signature is), so it is safe to echo back for admin visibility.

    `payload_template` is a partial exception: it isn't itself a SecretStore-
    backed credential column, but an admin authoring one (e.g. a PagerDuty
    Events-API body) commonly has nowhere else to put that receiver's static
    routing/integration key than as a literal in the template JSON — which
    functions as a credential even though the field's storage doesn't treat
    it as one (#1663 review). It's therefore only ever included for an
    Admin caller; every other authenticated user gets `has_payload_template`
    instead, the same presence-only shape already used for genuine secrets.
    """

    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    type: str
    has_webhook: bool
    email_recipients: str | None
    webhook_url: str | None = None
    has_hmac_secret: bool = False
    #: Populated ONLY by create/rotate, in the response of that one call — the
    #: plaintext HMAC signing key, shown exactly once. Never set by a read.
    hmac_secret: str | None = None
    #: Admin-only — see the class docstring. `None` for a non-admin caller
    #: regardless of whether a template is actually set; use
    #: `has_payload_template` to tell "unset" from "set but not shown".
    payload_template: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    has_payload_template: bool = False
    auth_header_name: str | None = None
    has_auth_header: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def from_model(
        cls,
        channel: NotificationChannel,
        *,
        hmac_secret: str | None = None,
        include_payload_template: bool = True,
    ) -> ChannelRead:
        return cls(
            id=channel.id,
            name=channel.name,
            type=channel.type,
            has_webhook=channel.webhook_secret_ref is not None,
            email_recipients=channel.email_recipients,
            webhook_url=channel.webhook_url,
            has_hmac_secret=channel.hmac_secret_ref is not None,
            hmac_secret=hmac_secret,
            payload_template=channel.payload_template if include_payload_template else None,
            has_payload_template=channel.payload_template is not None,
            auth_header_name=channel.auth_header_name,
            has_auth_header=channel.auth_header_secret_ref is not None,
        )

@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ("member", "viewer"))
def test_payload_template_is_hidden_from_non_admin_readers(
    client: TestClient, as_role: Any, role: str
) -> None:
    """The template may embed a receiver's literal routing/integration key
    (the PR's own PagerDuty worked example does exactly this) — a non-admin
    must never read it back, only know one is set.
    """
    _admin, admin_headers = as_role("admin")
    created = client.post(
        "/api/v1/notification-channels",
        json={
            "name": "PagerDuty",
            "type": "webhook",
            "webhook_url": _WEBHOOK_URL,
            "payload_template": _TEMPLATE,
        },
        headers=admin_headers,
    ).json()
    _, headers = as_role(role)

    listed = client.get("/api/v1/notification-channels", headers=headers)
    row = next(c for c in listed.json() if c["id"] == created["id"])
    assert row["payload_template"] is None
    assert row["has_payload_template"] is True

    got = client.get(f"/api/v1/notification-channels/{created['id']}", headers=headers)
    assert got.json()["payload_template"] is None
    assert got.json()["has_payload_template"] is True

## Summary
`get_notification_config` reports `has_email_recipients: false` / `email_recipients_source: null` on a deployment where email alerts **are being delivered** — the exact "who gets told when orders fails → nobody" false answer this tool was originally fixed to prevent, recurring through a narrower gap.

## Root cause
`backend/app/mcp/server.py:1489-1491` gates on all three:
```python
smtp_ready = bool(settings.email_username and settings.email_password_secret_name and settings.email_from)
```
But `EmailPublisher` does **not** require `email_from`:
- `backend/app/core/config.py:271` — `email_from: str | None = None  # defaults to email_username when unset`
- `backend/app/alerting/email.py:239` — `self._sender = sender or username`
- `backend/app/alerting/email.py:246` — `if not (self._username and self._password_secret_name and self._sender): return` — `self._sender` is already `username` when `email_from` is unset, so this never fails on `email_from`.

## Impact
A deployment that sets `EMAIL_USERNAME` + `EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME` and relies on the documented sender fallback is actively emailing every alert (From: <EMAIL_USERNAME>) to `EMAIL_TO`/per-suite recipients. input.command:
gh issue create --title "security(llm): RCA narrative sends raw observed/expected values to the LLM provider, bypassing G3 redaction" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
The two established LLM features (`sql_generation`, `check_suggestion`) build their prompt exclusively through `llm_prompt_context.masked_profile_for_prompt`, which applies the G3 governance-floor mask before anything reaches the model. `rca_narrative` (#1633) does not go through this path at all.

## Evidence
- `backend/app/services/llm_rca.py`'s `_render_evidence` (~lines 245-266) puts `failing.get("observed_value")` and `failing.get("expected_value")` verbatim into the prompt, plus `metric_trend`, `check_history`, `sibling_checks`, `same_asset_siblings`, `upstream_pipeline_run`, `downstream_blast_radius` — none of it routed through `sensitive_profile_columns`/`mask_profile_columns` (the G3 machinery) or `run_service.redact_observed_value` (the column-aware redaction ladder every other results surface uses).
- `incident_evidence.build_evidence` (called from `incident_service.py`) is built once at incident-open time straight off the raw `Result` row. The only filtering applied, `incident_evidence._strip_sample_lists`, removes `partial_unexpected_list`/`unexpected_index_list` — keys that live in the separate `sample_failures` column, not in `observed_value`. It is a no-op for the actual shape `observed_value` takes (per `gx_runner.py`'s `_bounded_observed_value`).
- `observed_value` can itself be a literal cell value for range-style expectations (`expect_column_min_to_be_between`/`_max_to_be_between`, see `run_service.py`'s redaction logic for exactly this case) — i.e. real warehouse data, potentially PII, can reach the external model provider unmasked.

## Impact
An RCA narrative for a failing min/max-style check (or any check whose `observed_value` carries a literal value or list) sends that value to whichever external LLM provider the admin has configured, with none of the redaction the rest of the product enforces everywhere else results are surfaced (REST, MCP, alerts).

## Fix
Route RCA evidence-building through the same masking machinery `llm_prompt_context.masked_profile_for_prompt` / `run_service.redact_observed_value` already provide, rather than reading the raw `Result` row. Needs the column-policy/tags context available at evidence-build time (`incident_evidence.build_evidence` currently doesn't take it) — a real design/plumbing task, not a one-line fix, hence filed rather than patched inline.

Found while reviewing PR #1725/#1771 (compliance-doc accuracy for the outbound-LLM transfer vector) — the doc text being corrected there was copied from `admin.py`'s `_llm_intelligence_transfer` posture endpoint, which makes the same "masked aggregate profiler statistics — never sample rows" claim; that claim is accurate for `sql_generation`/`check_suggestion` but not for `rca_narrative`. The doc PR describes the two accurately-redacted paths without repeating the RCA overclaim; `admin.py`'s own text should be corrected once this is fixed.
EOF
)" --label "bug,security,priority/P1" 2>&1

## Summary
Every feature-kind LLM call (`sql_generation`, `check_suggestion`, `rca_narrative`) always lands a terminal-state row in `llm_invocations` via `execute_invocation` (claim → running → succeeded/failed/superseded) — but `POST /admin/llm/test` does not go through that path at all.

## Evidence
`admin.py`'s LLM-test route calls `llm_service.test_settings`, which calls `provider.complete("Reply with the single word: ok", ...)` directly against the live (or draft) provider endpoint — a genuine outbound LLM round-trip — with no `LlmInvocation` row created anywhere in that function.

## Impact
The compliance claim "every call is recorded with requester and token counts" (`admin.py`'s `_llm_intelligence_transfer` posture text, and the compliance docs corrected in #1725/#1771) is not literally true: any workspace admin can trigger a live call to the configured (or draft-configured, even before `enabled=true`) provider endpoint that leaves zero trace in the audit table. The prompt is fixed and non-data ("reply with the single word: ok"), so the privacy exposure is low, but it's a real gap in the "every call is recorded" claim and in `llm_invocations` as a complete usage ledger.

## Fix
Either route the test probe through `execute_invocation` too (a synthetic invocation kind), or narrow the compliance claim to "every feature invocation" rather than "every call," and note the connection-test probe separately (the same pattern already used for datasource connection tests, which are documented as not persisting a result).

Found during PR #1725/#1771 review (compliance-doc accuracy for the outbound-LLM transfer vector).
EOF

    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any

    """Recipients alone deliver nothing: `EmailPublisher.publish` no-ops unless the

Review the diff to `backend/app/mcp/server.py` on the current git branch (`fix/1724-mcp-email-smtp-gate`, diffed against `main`) for MCP tool-honesty issues.

        # workspace default configured.
        linked_channels = channel_service.list_channels_for_suite(session, sid)

            c.type == "teams" and c.webhook_secret_ref for c in linked_channels
        )
        has_slack_channel = any(
            c.type == "slack" and c.webhook_secret_ref for c in linked_channels
        )
        has_email_channel = any(c.type == "email" and c.email_recipients for c in linked_channels)

        def _channel(

gh issue create --title "mcp: reusable notification channels (#1514/#1662/#1663) have no MCP tool coverage at all" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Reusable notification channels (Teams/Slack/email/generic-webhook, #1514/#1662/#1663) have full REST CRUD but zero MCP tools. Found while extending `get_notification_config` to recognize a suite-linked channel as a third alert-configuration source (\`*_source: \"channel\"\`) — that new value has no companion tool an LLM client could call to find out *which* channel it is, or what type.

## Impact
An LLM client asking "who gets told when orders fails?" via `get_notification_config` can now correctly see `email_recipients_source: "channel"` (a linked reusable channel is why email delivers) but has no way to identify or inspect that channel — no `list_channels`, no `get_channel`, no `list_channels_for_suite` equivalent exists on the MCP surface.

## Fix
Add read-only MCP tools mirroring the REST read surface: something like `list_notification_channels` (workspace-wide) and `list_suite_channels` (suite-scoped), following the same "presence not value" discipline already established for webhook/HMAC secrets in this codebase (never resolve or return a credential — `has_webhook`, `has_hmac_secret`, `has_auth_header` style booleans only). Mutation tools (create/update/delete/link/unlink) are a separate, later decision — the #1514/#1662/#1663 work already establishes admin-gating and credential-redaction conventions to follow if/when that's added.

Found during PR #1774 (get_notification_config's SMTP-gate fix) review.
EOF
)" --label "priority/P3" 2>&1

    beside the suite override and the workspace default — `TeamsPublisher.publish`

def resolve_webhook_channels(
    session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, *, secret_store: SecretStore
) -> list[WebhookDestination]:
    """Every distinct :class:`WebhookDestination` for the suite's linked
    ``webhook`` channels — a channel missing the URL or the HMAC signing key
    (never configured, or the secret has gone missing) is skipped and logged,
    same fail-soft posture as :func:`resolve_channel_webhooks`, which this also
    matches by deduping on URL (two channels that happen to point at the same
    destination deliver once, not twice). The signing key never leaves the
    process except as an HMAC digest.

    An unresolvable AUTH HEADER secret is a softer failure than a missing HMAC
    key: the header is an extra, optional layer some receivers want beside the
    signature, not the thing securing the request, so the destination still
    delivers — just without that header — rather than being dropped entirely.
    """
    destinations: list[WebhookDestination] = []
    seen_urls: set[str] = set()
    for channel in list_channels_for_suite(session, suite_id):
        if channel.type != "webhook" or not channel.webhook_url or not channel.hmac_secret_ref:
            continue
        if channel.webhook_url in seen_urls:
            continue
        try:
            hmac_secret = secret_store.get(channel.hmac_secret_ref)
        except SecretNotFoundError:
            log.warning("notification_channel_hmac_unresolved", channel_id=str(channel.id))
            continue
        auth_header_value: str | None = None
        if channel.auth_header_name and channel.auth_header_secret_ref:
            try:
                auth_header_value = secret_store.get(channel.auth_header_secret_ref)
            except SecretNotFoundError:
                log.warning(
                    "notification_channel_auth_header_unresolved", channel_id=str(channel.id)
                )
        seen_urls.add(channel.webhook_url)
        destinations.append(
            WebhookDestination(
                url=channel.webhook_url,
                hmac_secret=hmac_secret,
                payload_template=channel.payload_template,
                auth_header_name=channel.auth_header_name if auth_header_value else None,
                auth_header_value=auth_header_value,
            )
        )
    return destinations

Review the uncommitted changes to backend/app/mcp/server.py (function get_notification_config) and its test file backend/tests/mcp/test_mcp_tools.py, on branch fix/1724-mcp-email-smtp-gate in /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ. Context: this PR (#1774) already fixed the SMTP-gate over-requirement (#1724) and a suite-linked-notification-channel blind spot. A follow-up /code-review pass on the PR found two more real gaps in the same tool, which I just fixed:

2. Teams/Slack/Email publishers deliver to the UNION of the suite-or-workspace primary destination AND any linked channel of the same type (confirmed in teams.py/slack.py/email.py: `webhooks = [primary, *channel_webhooks]`) — not either/or. The existing `_channel()` helper picked only ONE source label (suite > workspace > channel), which hid the case where a suite has both an override AND a linked channel simultaneously delivering. Fixed by adding three new independent boolean fields — `webhook_channel_linked`, `slack_webhook_channel_linked`, `email_recipients_channel_linked` — that report channel presence regardless of what `*_source` says, plus docstring changes explaining the two fields must be read together for additive delivery.

gh pr edit 1774 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- **#1724:** `smtp_ready` required `email_from` in addition to `email_username`/`email_password_secret_name`, so a suite using `EmailPublisher`'s documented `sender or username` fallback (no explicit `EMAIL_FROM`) was reported as having no email channel at all, even though delivery actually works.
- **Review round 1 (same tool):** `get_notification_config`'s webhook/Slack/email presence checks only considered the suite override and the workspace default — missing the third source, a reusable `NotificationChannel` (#1514/#1662/#1663) linked to the suite. All three publishers fan out to linked channels too, so a suite relying solely on one was reported as having no channel configured at all.
- **Review round 2 (same tool, two more gaps):**
  1. A 4th `NotificationChannel` type, `"webhook"` (generic HMAC-signed, #1662/#1663), has no suite/workspace fallback of its own and was never reported at all — a suite relying solely on one read as having nothing configured.
  2. Teams/Slack/Email publishers deliver to the **union** of the suite-or-workspace primary and every linked channel of the same type (`[primary, *channel_webhooks]`), not either/or — the single-source `_channel()` pick hid the case where both are simultaneously active.

## Changes
- `smtp_ready` narrowed to `email_username and email_password_secret_name`.
- `_channel()` gains a `channel_configured` kwarg and a new `"channel"` `*_source` value, wired via `channel_service.list_channels_for_suite` (presence-only — the secret store is never read).
- New `has_generic_webhooks` field for the 4th channel type, named to avoid colliding with `has_webhook` (Teams).
- Three new independent boolean fields — `webhook_channel_linked` / `slack_webhook_channel_linked` / `email_recipients_channel_linked` — reported regardless of `*_source`, so additive delivery (override + linked channel both active) is visible.
- Docstring rewritten to name all sources up front and spell out the additive-delivery combination concretely, not just abstractly.

## Tests
7 new/expanded regression tests across both review rounds. All mutation-verified: each fix reverted to its pre-fix behavior inline, confirmed the right test fails for the right reason, restored to green.

## Verification
- `black --check` / `ruff check` / `mypy` — clean
- `bandit -r backend/app/mcp/server.py` — 0 issues
- `pytest backend/tests/mcp/` — 262 passed
- Full backend suite — 5613 passed, 10 skipped, 97.03% coverage
- `mcp-honesty-reviewer` — clean pass on both rounds

Fixes #1724

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1

reliability(llm): reaper thresholds mis-calibrated — pending false-kill under queue backlog + running false-reap during checksuggest warehouse profiling
---
Two distinct ways the #1644 reaper fails a **healthy** LLM invocation and reports a **false** cause. The reaper's compensating logic is correct; its thresholds don't account for real latency.

## Part A — pending false-kill under a shared-queue backlog (MAJOR)
There is no Celery task routing: `backend/app/worker/celery_app.py` `conf.update` sets no `task_routes`/`task_default_queue`, and `backend/app/services/run_dispatch.py:43,48` sends **both** `llm_invoke` and `run_suite` to the one default FIFO queue. The worker is single-replica prefork with small concurrency and `task_acks_late=False`.

A backlog of long `run_suite` tasks (this deployment class has large UC suites — the local DB literally has 1M–200M-row perf suites) leaves an `llm_invoke` message **queued in the broker** past the 15-min pending cutoff. `llm_service.reap_stuck_invocations` (`:452-460`) then fails it with *"the dispatch was likely lost before a worker claimed it"* — **false; the message is intact**. When the worker finally pulls it, the claim (`:298-306`, guard `status=='pending'`) finds `failed` and returns `skipped`. The user's request is **permanently dead with a false diagnosis**, precisely when the system was merely busy.

Fix options: a dedicated queue for `llm_invoke`; or a larger pending threshold; or wording that admits the "waiting in a shared queue" ambiguity. (Distinct from #1717, which is the reaper's unindexed scan.)

## Part B — running false-reap during checksuggest's warehouse leg (MINOR-MAJOR)
`backend/app/core/config.py:119-121` justifies the 10-min running threshold as "margin above the 120s provider timeout", but:
- `AnthropicProvider` is built with `max_retries=1` (`anthropic_provider.py:38`) → up to ~240s of provider time.
- The **checksuggest** builder does live warehouse work *inside* `running`: `list_columns` + a full `profile_connection` with `top_n=5` across all columns (sqlgen deliberately skips this with `top_n=0`).

Cold/suspended-warehouse resume + wide-table top-values profile + 240s LLM can plausibly cross 10 min → a HEALTHY invocation is reaped as *"the worker never finished — likely killed mid-call"*, its genuine result discarded (`superseded`), and the billed tokens exist **only in a log line** — not on the `llm_invocations` row the ADR-0042 G4 cost/audit posture rests on.

Found in a full-codebase QA sweep; Part A confirmed by mechanism, Part B plausible.

gh issue create --title "reliability(llm): dedicated Celery queue for llm_invoke so it doesn't queue behind long run_suite backlogs" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Split out from #1726 Part A. The reaper-threshold fix in #1726 (raising `llm_invocation_pending_threshold_minutes` + honest reap-reason wording) reduces false-kills but can't eliminate them: `run_dispatch.py` sends both `llm_invoke` and `run_suite` via `celery_app.send_task(...)` with no `queue=` argument, and `celery_app.py`'s `conf.update` sets no `task_routes`/`task_default_queue` — both task types share the single default Celery queue, FIFO. A backlog of long `run_suite` tasks (this deployment class has 1M-200M-row UC perf suites) can leave an `llm_invoke` message queued-but-intact past any static pending threshold.

The structurally correct fix is a dedicated queue for `llm_invoke` (`task_routes = {"llm_invoke": {"queue": "llm"}}`), so Celery round-robins fairly across queues from a single worker rather than draining one FIFO queue strictly in arrival order. Scoped out of #1726 because it's a deploy-coordination hazard, not just an app-code change: the worker is started with no `-Q` flag (`celery -A backend.app.worker.celery_app worker -B`, in `docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/terraform/azure/containerapps.tf` AND `deploy/terraform/aws/ecs.tf`), defaulting to consuming only the default queue. Routing `llm_invoke` onto a new queue name requires the worker command to also add `-Q celery,llm` (or equivalent) in all three places — and per the AWS README's own recorded gotcha, an ECS task-def command change needs an explicit `tofu apply -replace` (task defs `ignore_changes[container_definitions]`), not just an image roll. Shipping the routing change without the worker-command change deployed in the same coordinated step would silently stop ALL `llm_invoke` processing (nothing consuming the new queue) until the IaC apply catches up — exactly the deploy-ordering class of incident this project's history (#1355, #1373, #1361) already warns about.

Needs: the `task_routes` change, the worker-command change in all three deploy targets, and an explicit note in the PR description (or `deploy/README.md`) calling out that the Terraform command-array change requires `-replace` on AWS, not just an image roll — verified live on both clouds after deploy, per the #953 rule (a queue a worker isn't consuming is invisible to every test that runs against a fully-configured worker fixture).
EOF
)" 2>&1

fix(llm): reaper thresholds mis-calibrated + honest reap-reason wording

Two distinct ways the #1644 reaper failed a healthy invocation and
reported a false cause (found in a full-codebase QA sweep, #1726):

Part A — pending false-kill under a shared-queue backlog. There is no
Celery task routing: run_dispatch.py sends both llm_invoke and
run_suite via send_task with no queue argument, and celery_app.py's
conf.update sets no task_routes. A backlog of long run_suite tasks
(this deployment class has 1M-200M-row UC perf suites) can leave an
llm_invoke message queued-but-intact in the broker past the 15m
pending cutoff — the reaper then fails it as "the dispatch was likely
lost", false, and the worker's later claim attempt finds the row
already failed and returns skipped. The request is permanently dead
with a false diagnosis exactly when the system was merely busy.

Part B — running false-reap during checksuggest's warehouse leg. The
10m running threshold was margin above only the 120s provider timeout,
but execute_invocation calls the kind builder AFTER marking the row
running, and the check-suggestion builder does live warehouse work
(list_columns + a full profile, top_n=5) inside that window. A cold/
suspended warehouse resume plus a wide-table profile plus the
provider's own worst case (120s timeout x up to 2 attempts,
max_retries=1) can plausibly cross 10m for a healthy call.

Fix: raised both defaults (pending 15->30m, running 10->20m) with the
reasoning now recorded in config.py, and reworded both reap reasons to
admit the ambiguity a static threshold can never fully resolve — no
celery task id is stored on the row to check the broker directly, so
neither reap can prove "dead" vs. "queued"/"slow". The deeper fix for
Part A, a dedicated Celery queue for llm_invoke, is scoped out as
#1777: it needs the worker command changed in three deploy targets
(docker-compose.yml + both clouds' Terraform) in the same coordinated
step as the routing change, or an app-code-only deploy would silently
stop all llm_invoke processing until the IaC catches up.

Two new regression tests, mutation-verified: the default-threshold
test fails against the pre-fix 15/10 values, and the wording test
fails against the pre-fix strings — both confirmed to fail for the
right reason, then restored to green.
EOF
)" 2>&1

gh pr create --title "fix(llm): reaper thresholds mis-calibrated + honest reap-reason wording" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Two distinct ways the #1644 reaper fails a **healthy** LLM invocation and reports a **false** cause, found in a full-codebase QA sweep (#1726).

**Part A — pending false-kill under a shared-queue backlog.** No Celery task routing exists: `run_dispatch.py` sends both `llm_invoke` and `run_suite` via `send_task` with no `queue=` argument, and `celery_app.py`'s `conf.update` sets no `task_routes`. A backlog of long `run_suite` tasks (this deployment class has 1M-200M-row UC perf suites) can leave an `llm_invoke` message queued-but-intact past the 15m pending cutoff, which the reaper then fails as "the dispatch was likely lost" — false. The worker's later claim finds the row already `failed` and returns `skipped`: the request is permanently dead with a false diagnosis exactly when the system was merely busy.

**Part B — running false-reap during checksuggest's warehouse leg.** The 10m running threshold was margin above only the 120s provider timeout, but `execute_invocation` calls the kind builder AFTER marking the row `running`, and the check-suggestion builder does live warehouse work (`list_columns` + a full profile, `top_n=5`) inside that window. A cold/suspended warehouse resume plus a wide-table profile plus the provider's own worst case (120s timeout × up to 2 attempts, `max_retries=1`) can plausibly cross 10m for a healthy call.

## Fix
- Raised both defaults: pending 15→30m, running 10→20m, with the reasoning recorded in `config.py`.
- Reworded both reap reasons to admit the ambiguity a static threshold can never fully resolve — no celery task id is stored on the row to check the broker directly, so neither reap can prove "dead" vs. "queued"/"slow".
- Filed [#1777](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1777) for the structurally correct Part-A fix (a dedicated Celery queue for `llm_invoke`) — deliberately scoped out here because it needs the worker command changed in three deploy targets (`docker-compose.yml` + both clouds' Terraform) in the same coordinated step as the routing change, or an app-code-only deploy would silently stop all `llm_invoke` processing until the IaC catches up.

## Tests
2 new regression tests, mutation-verified: the default-threshold test reverted against the pre-fix 15/10 values, the wording test reverted against the pre-fix strings — both confirmed to fail for the right reason, then restored to green.

## Verification
- `black --check` / `ruff check` / `mypy` — clean
- `bandit -r backend/app/core/config.py backend/app/services/llm_service.py` — 0 issues
- `pytest backend/tests/services/test_llm_reaper.py backend/tests/worker/test_llm_reaper_task.py` — 10 passed
- Full backend suite — 5618 passed, 10 skipped, 97.03% coverage

Fixes #1726

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1

input.command:
gh pr edit 1778 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Two distinct ways the #1644 reaper fails a **healthy** LLM invocation and reports a **false** cause, found in a full-codebase QA sweep (#1726).

**Part A — pending false-kill under a shared-queue backlog.** No Celery task routing exists: `run_dispatch.py` sends both `llm_invoke` and `run_suite` via `send_task` with no `queue=` argument, and `celery_app.py`'s `conf.update` sets no `task_routes`. A backlog of long `run_suite` tasks (this deployment class has 1M-200M-row UC perf suites) can leave an `llm_invoke` message queued-but-intact past the 15m pending cutoff, which the reaper then fails as "the dispatch was likely lost" — false. The worker's later claim finds the row already `failed` and returns `skipped`: the request is permanently dead with a false diagnosis exactly when the system was merely busy.

**Part B — running false-reap during checksuggest's warehouse leg.** The 10m running threshold was margin above only the 120s provider timeout, but `execute_invocation` calls the kind builder AFTER marking the row `running`, and the check-suggestion builder does live warehouse work (`list_columns` + a full profile, `top_n=5`) inside that window. A cold/suspended warehouse resume plus a wide-table profile plus the provider's own worst case (120s timeout × up to 2 attempts, `max_retries=1`) can plausibly cross 10m for a healthy call.

## Fix
- Raised both defaults: pending 15→30m, running 10→20m, with the reasoning recorded in `config.py`.
- Reworded both reap reasons to admit the ambiguity a static threshold can never fully resolve — no celery task id is stored on the row to check the broker directly, so neither reap can prove "dead" vs. "queued"/"slow".
- Filed [#1777](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1777) for the structurally correct Part-A fix (a dedicated Celery queue for `llm_invoke`) — deliberately scoped out here because it needs the worker command changed in three deploy targets (`docker-compose.yml` + both clouds' Terraform) in the same coordinated step as the routing change, or an app-code-only deploy would silently stop all `llm_invoke` processing until the IaC catches up.

## Review round 2
`/code-review` found the code-level fix hadn't propagated to what actually ships a fresh stack: `.env.app.example` carries these two keys **active** (not blank like most optional keys), and `setup.sh` copies it verbatim into every new `.env.app`, which `pydantic-settings` reads ahead of the code default — so every fresh local/dev/eval environment would have silently kept the exact false-kill exposure this PR exists to close. Fixed the template and a stale beat-schedule comment citing the old 10-minute threshold; added a regression test that loads the template as `Settings` (mirroring the file's own existing #1072 pattern) and asserts its values equal the code default, so either side drifting alone now fails it.

## Tests
3 new regression tests total, all mutation-verified: the default-threshold test reverted against the pre-fix 15/10 code values, the wording test reverted against the pre-fix strings, and the template-drift test reverted against the pre-fix template values — all three confirmed to fail for the right reason, then restored to green.

## Verification
- `black --check` / `ruff check` / `mypy` — clean
- `bandit -r backend/app/core/config.py backend/app/services/llm_service.py` — 0 issues
- Full backend suite — 5618 passed, 10 skipped, 97.03% coverage (plus the review-round follow-ups re-verified separately)

Fixes #1726

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1
